Benefactor

/BEN-uh-fak-ter/ - the stress falls on BEN · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Benefactor means a person who gives money or help to a person or cause.

A brass plaque in the lobby thanks the benefactor whose gift built the skating rink and whose visits kept it open.

Worked Example

The town band owned two dented trumpets until Mr. Aoki retired from his orchard. He bought the band a full set of instruments, then kept showing up — driving the tuba to away games, paying for repairs, teaching the youngest players to oil their valves. Money was only half of what he gave.

Benefactor is the exact word for Mr. Aoki, because a benefactor is a person who gives money or help to a person or cause — the definition holds both halves of what he did. Donor is narrower: a donor writes the check, and one check is enough; a benefactor's support tends to keep arriving.

How Benefactor Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

patron

patron: backs artists or institutions, often expecting a little credit

donor

donor: anyone who gives once — a benefactor's giving tends to continue

Antonyms

beneficiary

beneficiary: the receiver of the gift — the mirror image

freeloader

freeloader: takes support endlessly and gives nothing back

How Strong Is It? — supporter → donor → benefactor

supporter vs. benefactor

supporter vs. benefactor: A supporter may give nothing but applause — signing the petition and cheering from the sidelines already earns the name.

donor vs. benefactor

donor vs. benefactor: A donor goes further than a supporter — money actually changes hands — but a single gift is enough to be a donor, while a benefactor keeps a person or cause afloat.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of benefactor.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — bene

Root — bene: well, good (Latin)

Root — fact

Root — fact: to do, to make (Latin facere)

Suffix — -or

Suffix — -or: one who

Put it together

Put it together: Bene (well) + fact (do, make) + -or (one who) = one who does good. Latin benefactor was literally a 'well-doer,' and the English word keeps the whole recipe in plain sight: a benefactor is someone who does good for a person or a cause, with money or with help.

Use the root in a new word: factory

Use the root in a new word: factory: A factory is literally a place of making — the same fact root, busy at its plainest work.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / appreciative

Benefactor names the person behind the giving. Keep the family straight: benevolent describes the kindly disposition, largess and munificence describe the giving itself, and bequeath is how a benefactor gives one last time — through a will. Use benefactor when you mean the human being a cause could thank.
